## Why not keep growing?

Everything a cell takes in or gives out must cross its surface, and every part inside depends on that supply. Two things matter, then: how much surface a cell has, and how much inside that surface must serve. We use a cube here because it is easy to count.

<!-- STEP -->
## Double the width

Press **Double the width**. The cube is 2 units wide now. Its surface is 4 times as large, but its inside is 8 times as large, so each part of the inside has less surface to serve it.

<!-- STEP -->
## Many small cells

Press **Split into small cells**. The same 8 units of inside are now 8 small cubes, and together they have 2 times the surface of the large cube.

**Small cells have more surface for what is inside them.**

<!-- STEP -->
## A model, not a measurement

These cubes are a model and do not measure a real cell. They show one reason why cells stay small, and why a cell holds many small mitochondria and not one giant one. A growing body gets its new cells in one way only, and that is by division.
